claim: Mutations of SLC26A4 are a common cause of hearing loss associated with enlargement of the endolymphatic sac (EES).
source: Mutations of SLC26A4 are a common cause of hearing loss associated with enlargement of the endolymphatic sac (EES).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Slc26a4 expression in the developing mouse endolymphatic sac is required for acquisition of normal inner ear structure and function.
source: Slc26a4 expression in the developing mouse endolymphatic sac is required for acquisition of normal inner ear structure and function.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by previous studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: The mouse endolymphatic sac absorbs fluid in an SLC26A4-dependent fashion.
source: Here, we show that the mouse endolymphatic sac absorbs fluid in an SLC26A4-dependent fashion.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the in vitro fluid absorption experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Fluid absorption by the endolymphatic sac was sensitive to ouabain.
source: Fluid absorption was sensitive to ouabain and gadolinium but insensitive to benzamil, bafilomycin and S3226.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Fluid absorption by the endolymphatic sac was sensitive to gadolinium.
source: Fluid absorption was sensitive to ouabain and gadolinium but insensitive to benzamil, bafilomycin and S3226.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Fluid absorption by the endolymphatic sac was insensitive to benzamil.
source: Fluid absorption was sensitive to ouabain and gadolinium but insensitive to benzamil, bafilomycin and S3226.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Fluid absorption by the endolymphatic sac was insensitive to bafilomycin.
source: Fluid absorption was sensitive to ouabain and gadolinium but insensitive to benzamil, bafilomycin and S3226.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Fluid absorption by the endolymphatic sac was insensitive to S3226.
source: Fluid absorption was sensitive to ouabain and gadolinium but insensitive to benzamil, bafilomycin and S3226.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of pre- and postnatal endolymphatic sacs demonstrates two types of differentiated cells.
source: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of pre- and postnatal endolymphatic sacs demonstrates two types of differentiated cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by PCA and hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: Early ribosome-rich cells (RRCs) have a transcriptomic signature suggesting expression and secretion of extracellular proteins.
source: Early ribosome-rich cells (RRCs) have a transcriptomic signature suggesting expression and secretion of extracellular proteins, while mature RRCs express genes implicated in innate immunity.
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 2E and differential expression analysis.

claim: Mature RRCs express genes implicated in innate immunity.
source: Early ribosome-rich cells (RRCs) have a transcriptomic signature suggesting expression and secretion of extracellular proteins, while mature RRCs express genes implicated in innate immunity.
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis and differential expression of genes at P30 shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The transcriptomic signature of mitochondria-rich cells (MRCs) indicates that they mediate vectorial ion transport.
source: The transcriptomic signature of mitochondria-rich cells (MRCs) indicates that they mediate vectorial ion transport.
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 2D and expression of ion transport genes shown in Figure 7 and Table 1.

claim: Disruption of the NaCl resorption mechanism in MRCs is the root cause of hearing loss associated with EES.
source: We propose a molecular mechanism for resorption of NaCl by MRCs during development, and conclude that disruption of this mechanism is the root cause of hearing loss associated with EES.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the integration of functional data, transcriptomic analysis, and gene array data.

claim: Enlargement of the vestibular aqueduct (EVA) is the most commonly detected osseous malformation of the inner ear in children with sensorineural hearing loss.
source: Enlargement of the vestibular aqueduct (EVA; OMIM 600791) is the most commonly detected osseous malformation of the inner ear in children with sensorineural hearing loss (Griffith and Wangemann, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Griffith and Wangemann, 2011.

claim: The enlargement of the vestibular aqueduct is not considered to be the direct cause of hearing loss.
source: The enlargement of the vestibular aqueduct is not considered to be the direct cause of hearing loss (Griffith and Wangemann, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Griffith and Wangemann, 2011.

claim: The endolymphatic sac is an evolutionarily conserved structure present even in the primitive inner ear of hagfish.
source: The endolymphatic sac is an evolutionarily conserved structure present even in the primitive inner ear of hagfish (Jørgensen et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jørgensen et al., 1998.

claim: The endolymphatic sac is the first structure to develop from the otocyst during early organogenesis.
source: Moreover, the endolymphatic sac is the first structure to develop from the otocyst during early organogenesis (Raft et al., 2014; Morsli et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Raft et al., 2014 and Morsli et al., 1998.

claim: The embryonic endolymphatic sac engages in NaCl resorption and the ensuing fluid resorption is critical for morphogenesis of the inner ear.
source: Previous investigations suggest that the embryonic endolymphatic sac engages in NaCl resorption and that the ensuing fluid resorption is critical for morphogenesis of the inner ear and the progression of development leading to the acquisition of hearing and vestibular function (Kim and Wangemann, 2010; Li et al., 2013a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim and Wangemann, 2010 and Li et al., 2013a.

claim: The rate of fluid absorption was higher in endolymphatic sacs from Slc26a4Δ/+ mice (12.3 ± 2.6 nl x hr−1 x mm−2, n = 26) than in endolymphatic sacs from Slc26a4Δ/Δ mice (6.0 ± 1.6 nl x hr−1 x mm−2, n = 12).
source: The rate of fluid absorption was higher in endolymphatic sacs from Slc26a4Δ/+ mice (12.3 ± 2.6 nl x hr−1 x mm−2, n = 26) than in endolymphatic sacs from Slc26a4Δ/Δ mice (6.0 ± 1.6 nl x hr−1 x mm−2, n = 12, One-way ANOVA: p<0.001, Cohens's d = 3.0; Figure 1—source data 1)
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and statistical analysis.

claim: The rate of fluid absorption in endolymphatic sacs from Slc26a4Δ/+ mice in the presence of ouabain (1 mM, 5.3 ± 1.8 nl x hr−1 x mm−2, n = 7) was significantly lower than without ouabain.
source: The rate of fluid absorption was higher in endolymphatic sacs from Slc26a4Δ/+ mice (12.3 ± 2.6 nl x hr−1 x mm−2, n = 26) than in endolymphatic sacs from Slc26a4Δ/Δ mice (6.0 ± 1.6 nl x hr−1 x mm−2, n = 12, One-way ANOVA: p<0.001, Cohens's d = 3.0; Figure 1—source data 1) or in endolymphatic sacs from Slc26a4Δ/+ mice in the presence of ouabain, a blocker of Na+/K+ ATPase (1 mM, 5.3 ± 1.8 nl x hr−1 x mm−2, n = 7, One-way ANOVA: p<0.001, Cohen's d = 3.2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and statistical analysis.

claim: ATP1A1, the alpha 1 subunit of Na+/K+ ATPase, was detected in basolateral membranes of all epithelial cells in the endolymphatic sac and duct.
source: Expression of ATP1A1, the alpha 1 subunit of Na+/K+ ATPase, was detected in basolateral membranes of all epithelial cells in the endolymphatic sac and duct (Figure 1E–G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1E-G.

claim: The addition of benzamil (10 µM or 100 µM) to the luminal fluid had no significant effect on the rate of fluid absorption in endolymphatic sacs of E14.5 Slc26a4Δ/+ mice.
source: Neither the addition of benzamil (10 µM or 100 µM, one-way ANOVA: p=1), the addition of bafilomycin A1 (10 nM or 10 µM, one-way ANOVA: p=1), nor the addition of S3226 (20 µM, one-way ANOVA: p=1) to the luminal fluid had a significant effect on the rate of fluid absorption in endolymphatic sacs of E14.5 Slc26a4Δ/+ mice.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data and statistical analysis.

claim: The addition of bafilomycin A1 (10 nM or 10 µM) to the luminal fluid had no significant effect on the rate of fluid absorption in endolymphatic sacs of E14.5 Slc26a4Δ/+ mice.
source: Neither the addition of benzamil (10 µM or 100 µM, one-way ANOVA: p=1), the addition of bafilomycin A1 (10 nM or 10 µM, one-way ANOVA: p=1), nor the addition of S3226 (20 µM, one-way ANOVA: p=1) to the luminal fluid had a significant effect on the rate of fluid absorption in endolymphatic sacs of E14.5 Slc26a4Δ/+ mice.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data and statistical analysis.

claim: The addition of S3226 (20 µM) to the luminal fluid had no significant effect on the rate of fluid absorption in endolymphatic sacs of E14.5 Slc26a4Δ/+ mice.
source: Neither the addition of benzamil (10 µM or 100 µM, one-way ANOVA: p=1), the addition of bafilomycin A1 (10 nM or 10 µM, one-way ANOVA: p=1), nor the addition of S3226 (20 µM, one-way ANOVA: p=1) to the luminal fluid had a significant effect on the rate of fluid absorption in endolymphatic sacs of E14.5 Slc26a4Δ/+ mice.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data and statistical analysis.

claim: The rate of fluid absorption was higher in endolymphatic sacs from Slc26a4Δ/+ mice in the absence (12.6 ± 2.7 nl x hr−1 x mm−2, n = 6) than in the presence of gadolinium (8.1 ± 1.5 nl x hr−1 x mm−2, n = 11).
source: The rate of fluid absorption was higher in endolymphatic sacs from Slc26a4Δ/+ mice in the absence (12.6 ± 2.7 nl x hr−1 x mm−2, n = 6) than in the presence of gadolinium (8.1 ± 1.5 nl x hr−1 x mm−2, n = 11, One-way ANOVA: p=0.008, Cohens's d = 2.2; Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and statistical analysis.

claim: Fluid absorption in the embryonic endolymphatic sac at E14.5 depends on SLC26A4, Na+/K+ ATPase, and a gadolinium-sensitive pathway.
source: Taken together, these observations demonstrate that fluid absorption in the embryonic endolymphatic sac at E14.5 depends on SLC26A4, Na+/K+ ATPase, and a gadolinium-sensitive pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data from the three groups of experiments.

claim: Neither v-ATPase, ENaC Na+ channels, nor the Na+/H+ exchanger NHE3 are required for fluid absorption at E14.5.
source: Neither v-ATPase, ENaC Na+ channels, nor the Na+/H+ exchanger NHE3 are required at this age.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the insensitivity of fluid absorption to bafilomycin, benzamil, and S3226.

claim: 82 P5 epithelial cells were selected for RNA-seq analysis.
source: We selected only clearly-identified single cells, leaving 82 P5 epithelial cells for RNA-seq analysis (Materials and methods, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the methods and results section.

claim: Principal component analysis (PCA) of the RNA-seq data separated cells into two distinct populations.
source: The first principal component (PC1) separated cells into two distinct populations in an unbiased fashion (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by PCA shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The canonical MRC markers (Slc26a4, Foxi1, Atp6v0a4, Atp6v1b1, Jag1, and Coch) showed high positive correlation with PC1.
source: The canonical MRC markers (Slc26a4, Foxi1, Atp6v0a4, Atp6v1b1, Jag1, and Coch) showed high positive correlation with PC1, whereas Notch1, which is the only known gene expression marker of embryonic non-MRCs (Raft et al., 2014), showed a negative correlation with PC1 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the correlation circle map shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Notch1 showed a negative correlation with PC1.
source: The canonical MRC markers (Slc26a4, Foxi1, Atp6v0a4, Atp6v1b1, Jag1, and Coch) showed high positive correlation with PC1, whereas Notch1, which is the only known gene expression marker of embryonic non-MRCs (Raft et al., 2014), showed a negative correlation with PC1 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the correlation circle map shown in Figure 2B and supported by a citation.

claim: Hierarchical clustering analysis using the 300 genes with the highest positive or negative correlation with PC1 exhibited clear segregation of each of the 82 cells into one of two primary clusters.
source: Hierarchical clustering analysis using the 300 genes with the highest positive or negative correlation with PC1 exhibited clear segregation of each of the 82 cells into one of two primary clusters, and segregation of each of the 300 genes into one of two primary clusters (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The two cell clusters at P5 were assigned to MRCs and RRCs based upon expression patterns of the canonical cell markers.
source: Based upon expression patterns of the canonical cell markers, the two cell clusters were assigned to P5 MRCs and P5 RRCs.
evidence: This is based on the hierarchical clustering and expression of known markers.

claim: 594 genes were differentially expressed in MRCs at P5 (FDR < 0.05, specificity score >0.5).
source: We identified 433 genes whose expression was specific to RRCs ('RRC genes') and 611 genes whose expression was specific to MRCs ('MRC genes') according to criteria of significant differential expression (false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05 and specificity >0.5) (Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and the data is provided in Figure 2—source data 2.

claim: 433 genes were differentially expressed in RRCs at P5 (FDR < 0.05, specificity score >0.5).
source: We identified 433 genes whose expression was specific to RRCs ('RRC genes') and 611 genes whose expression was specific to MRCs ('MRC genes') according to criteria of significant differential expression (false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05 and specificity >0.5) (Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and the data is provided in Figure 2—source data 2.

claim: Gene ontology terms enriched for P5 MRC genes included 'mitochondrion' (GO:0005739).
source: Gene ontology terms that were enriched for P5 MRC genes included 'mitochondrion' (GO:0005739) and other terms implicating mitochondrial function such as 'generation of precursor metabolites and energy' (GO:0006091) and 'respiratory electron transport chain' (GO:0022904).
evidence: This is demonstrated by gene ontology enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Gene ontology terms enriched for P5 MRC genes included 'generation of precursor metabolites and energy' (GO:0006091).
source: Gene ontology terms that were enriched for P5 MRC genes included 'mitochondrion' (GO:0005739) and other terms implicating mitochondrial function such as 'generation of precursor metabolites and energy' (GO:0006091) and 'respiratory electron transport chain' (GO:0022904).
evidence: This is demonstrated by gene ontology enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Gene ontology terms enriched for P5 MRC genes included 'respiratory electron transport chain' (GO:0022904).
source: Gene ontology terms that were enriched for P5 MRC genes included 'mitochondrion' (GO:0005739) and other terms implicating mitochondrial function such as 'generation of precursor metabolites and energy' (GO:0006091) and 'respiratory electron transport chain' (GO:0022904).
evidence: This is demonstrated by gene ontology enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: P5 RRC genes were significantly associated with the GO terms 'ribosome' (GO:0005840) and 'translation' (GO:0006412).
source: Postnatal day 5 RRC genes were significantly associated with the GO terms 'ribosome' (GO:0005840) and 'translation' (GO:0006412).
evidence: This is demonstrated by gene ontology enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering identified two cell populations among 46 P30 cells, which were readily assigned to MRCs or RRCs.
source: Principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering identified two cell populations among 46 P30 cells, which were readily assigned to MRCs or RRCs on the basis of canonical and putative population-specific genes identified by the P5 analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by PCA and hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: There is no qualitative difference in endolymphatic sac cellular composition between P5 and P30.
source: This result indicates that there is no qualitative difference in endolymphatic sac cellular composition between P5 and P30.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the similarity of cell populations identified at P5 and P30.

claim: 316 MRC-specific genes and 222 RRC-specific genes were identified at P30 (FDR < 0.05, specificity >0.5).
source: The subsequent differential expression analysis (FDR < 0.05, specificity >0.5) identified 316 MRC-specific genes and 222 RRC-specific genes at P30 (Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and the data is provided in Figure 2—source data 2.

claim: Four MRC-specific genes (Chchd10, Coch, Atp6v1g3, and Tnrc6b) showed significantly increasing expression at P30 in comparison to P5 (FDR < 0.05, specificity >0.65).
source: We identified four MRC-specific genes (Chchd10, Coch, Atp6v1g3, and Tnrc6b) and 9 RRC-specific genes (Slpi, Serping1, Cp, Clu, Sbsn, Trf, Sostdc1, Lcn2, and Rarres2) whose expression was significantly increasing at P30 in comparison to P5 (FDR < 0.05, specificity >0.65) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by differential expression analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Nine RRC-specific genes (Slpi, Serping1, Cp, Clu, Sbsn, Trf, Sostdc1, Lcn2, and Rarres2) showed significantly increasing expression at P30 in comparison to P5 (FDR < 0.05, specificity >0.65).
source: We identified four MRC-specific genes (Chchd10, Coch, Atp6v1g3, and Tnrc6b) and 9 RRC-specific genes (Slpi, Serping1, Cp, Clu, Sbsn, Trf, Sostdc1, Lcn2, and Rarres2) whose expression was significantly increasing at P30 in comparison to P5 (FDR < 0.05, specificity >0.65) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by differential expression analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: The nine genes whose expression was specific to P30 RRCs were associated with GO terms such as 'iron ion homeostasis' (GO:0055076), 'defense response' (GO:0006952), or 'innate immune response' (GO:0045087).
source: The nine genes whose expression was specific to P30 RRCs were associated with GO terms such as 'iron ion homeostasis' (GO:0055076; p-value 2.14 × 10−6; Cp, Trf, Lcn2), 'defense response' (GO:0006952; p-value 2.54 × 10−6; Lcn2, Rarres2, Slpi, Serping1, Trf), or 'innate immune response' (GO:0045087, p-value 7.22 × 10−4; Lcn2, Slpi, Serping1), implying that mature RRCs might contribute to immunity of the inner ear.
evidence: This is demonstrated by gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: Mature RRCs might contribute to immunity of the inner ear.
source: The nine genes whose expression was specific to P30 RRCs were associated with GO terms such as 'iron ion homeostasis' (GO:0055076; p-value 2.14 × 10−6; Cp, Trf, Lcn2), 'defense response' (GO:0006952; p-value 2.54 × 10−6; Lcn2, Rarres2, Slpi, Serping1, Trf), or 'innate immune response' (GO:0045087, p-value 7.22 × 10−4; Lcn2, Slpi, Serping1), implying that mature RRCs might contribute to immunity of the inner ear.
evidence: This is an inference based on gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: Approximately one half of P5 and P30 RRCs express Slc26a4 at a low level.
source: Interestingly, our single-cell RNA-seq data indicate that approximately one half of P5 and P30 RRCs express Slc26a4 at a low level (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by violin plots shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The mean expression levels of Slc26a4 in Slc26a4-positive RRCs (>5 log2 (nTPM)) are 14-to 18-fold lower than those for MRCs.
source: The mean expression levels of Slc26a4 in Slc26a4-positive RRCs (>5 log2 (nTPM)) are 14-to 18-fold lower than those for MRCs.
evidence: This is based on analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data.

claim: Single-cell qPCR of epithelial cells isolated from C57BL/6J P5 endolymphatic sacs confirmed that some cells expressed Slc26a4 but not other MRC-specific genes.
source: To validate the expression of Slc26a4 in the non-MRC cell population, we performed single-cell qPCR of epithelial cells isolated from C57BL/6J P5 endolymphatic sacs. Consistent with the result of single cell RNA-seq, we found that some cells expressed Slc26a4 but not other MRC-specific genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by single-cell qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Immunohistochemistry of P5 endolymphatic sacs verified the presence of SLC26A4 in ATP6V1B1-negative cells.
source: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) of P5 endolymphatic sacs verified the presence of SLC26A4 in ATP6V1B1-negative cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B) and FOXI1-negative cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Immunohistochemistry of P5 endolymphatic sacs verified the presence of SLC26A4 in FOXI1-negative cells.
source: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) of P5 endolymphatic sacs verified the presence of SLC26A4 in ATP6V1B1-negative cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B) and FOXI1-negative cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: A subset of RRCs express SLC26A4 at low levels.
source: These findings indicate that a subset of RRCs express SLC26A4 at low levels.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on single-cell RNA-seq, qPCR, and immunohistochemistry data.

claim: Principal component analysis did not identify any distinct clusters of E12.5 cells.
source: Principal component analysis did not identify any distinct clusters of E12.5 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is demonstrated by PCA shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: E16.5 cells were clustered into three populations.
source: Principal component analysis did not identify any distinct clusters of E12.5 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), whereas E16.5 cells were clustered into three populations (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by PCA and hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: The three E16.5 cell populations were assigned as MRCs, progenitor cells (ProgCs), and proliferating cells (ProlCs).
source: Thus, we designated the remaining cell populations as E16.5 progenitor cells (ProgCs) and E16.5 proliferating cells (ProlCs), respectively.
evidence: This is based on hierarchical clustering and gene expression patterns shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Differential expression testing between MRCs and ProgCs identified 975 E16.5 MRC genes and 278 E16.5 ProgC genes (FDR < 0.05, specificity >0.5).
source: Differential expression testing between MRCs and ProgCs identified 975 E16.5 MRC genes and 278 E16.5 ProgC genes (FDR < 0.05, specificity >0.5) (Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and the data is provided in Figure 2—source data 2.

claim: At E16.5, Foxi1 expression appeared to be less specific to MRCs than it was at P5 or P30.
source: At E16.5, Foxi1 expression appeared to be less specific to MRCs than it was at P5 or P30. In addition to high expression of Foxi1 in all MRCs, a subset of ProgCs and ProlCs also showed high expression levels of Foxi1 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A subset of ProgCs and ProlCs express other MRC genes, although the expression levels are lower than in MRCs.
source: In addition, we observed that some ProgCs and ProlCs express other MRC genes, although the expression levels are lower than in MRCs.
evidence: This is based on analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data.

claim: ProgCs and ProlCs expressing Foxi1 or other MRC genes represent a transitional state of progenitor cells that are proliferating and differentiating into MRCs.
source: From these observations, we hypothesized that ProgCs and ProlCs expressing Foxi1 or other MRC genes represent a transitional state of progenitor cells that are proliferating and differentiating into MRCs.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on gene expression patterns.

claim: PC2 clearly separates MRCs from other cells at all time points.
source: PC2 clearly separates MRCs from other cells at all time points (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by PCA shown in Figure 4A.

claim: PC3 segregates E12.5 cells.
source: PC3 segregates E12.5 cells and PC4 segregates E16.5 ProlCs from other cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by PCA shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: PC4 segregates E16.5 ProlCs from other cells.
source: PC3 segregates E12.5 cells and PC4 segregates E16.5 ProlCs from other cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by PCA shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Hierarchical clustering using 123 genes clustered the genes into five groups: MRC genes, early progenitor genes, proliferation genes, late RRC genes, and early RRC genes.
source: Each of the 123 genes were clustered into one of five groups: (1) genes specific to MRCs (MRC genes); (2) genes mainly specific to E12.5 cells (early progenitor genes); (3) genes specific to all E16.5 ProlCs, two P5 RRCs and one E12.5 cell (proliferation genes); (4) genes specific to E16.5 ProgCs and ProlCs, P5 RRCs and P30 RRCs (late RRC genes); and (5) genes specific to E12.5 cells, E16.5 ProgCs/ProlCs, and P5 RRCs (early RRC genes).
evidence: This is demonstrated by hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 4C.

claim: MRCs at all time points formed a single cluster.
source: Whereas MRCs at all time points formed a single cluster, E12.5 cells, E16.5 ProgCs, E16.5 ProlCs, P5 RRCs, and P30 RRCs formed another large cluster partially sharing expression profiles of early progenitor genes, early RRC genes, and late RRC genes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 4C.

claim: E12.5 cells, E16.5 ProgCs, E16.5 ProlCs, P5 RRCs, and P30 RRCs formed a large cluster partially sharing expression profiles of early progenitor genes, early RRC genes, and late RRC genes.
source: Whereas MRCs at all time points formed a single cluster, E12.5 cells, E16.5 ProgCs, E16.5 ProlCs, P5 RRCs, and P30 RRCs formed another large cluster partially sharing expression profiles of early progenitor genes, early RRC genes, and late RRC genes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 4C.

claim: E12.5 cells, E16.5 ProgCs, E16.5 ProlCs, P5 RRCs, and P30 RRCs constitute the main pathway of differentiation in endolymphatic sac epithelium.
source: This result suggests these latter cell groups constitute the main pathway of differentiation in endolymphatic sac epithelium.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on hierarchical clustering analysis.

claim: Only a few cells at E12.5 and P5 showed gene expression profiles associated with proliferation.
source: In addition, only a few cells at E12.5 and P5 showed gene expression profiles associated with proliferation, indicating proliferation may occur most actively at E16.5.
evidence: This is based on hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Proliferation may occur most actively at E16.5.
source: In addition, only a few cells at E12.5 and P5 showed gene expression profiles associated with proliferation, indicating proliferation may occur most actively at E16.5.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on gene expression profiles and supported by EdU labeling data.

claim: A maximal percentage of EdU-positive cells was detected at E16.5.
source: We tested this by counting 5-ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine (EdU)-positive cells, as a measure of proliferation, in whole mount samples of endolymphatic sac epithelium from E12.5 to P5 (Figure 5A). Our hypothesis was supported by a maximal percentage of EdU-positive cells detected at E16.5 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by EdU labeling data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: Monocle 2 ordered cells at E12.5, E16.5 and P5 in an unsupervised fashion and reconstructed a branched trajectory, beginning at E12.5 cells, passing through E16.5 ProlCs and ProgCs, and ending at two outcomes, P5 MRCs or P5 RRCs.
source: Monocle 2 ordered cells at E12.5, E16.5 and P5 in an unsupervised fashion and then reconstructed a branched trajectory, beginning at E12.5 cells, passing through E16.5 ProlCs and ProgCs, and ending at two outcomes, P5 MRCs or P5 RRCs (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by single-cell trajectory analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Six E16.5 ProgCs, one E16.5 ProlC, and two P5 RRCs were located along the MRC branch in the trajectory plot.
source: In the trajectory plot, six E16.5 ProgCs, one E16.5 ProlC, and two P5 RRCs were located along the MRC branch, indicating these cells are likely to be MRCs or progenitor cells for MRCs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by single-cell trajectory analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Along the MRC trajectory, mRNA levels of MRC genes such as Foxi1, Slc26a4, and Tfcp2l1 are increased.
